name: Headless runtime mismatches
plain: A few page details look odd when a browser has no real window or desktop.
meaning: Older headless Chrome showed an empty plugin list, no languages, a zero outer window size and a notification setting that disagreed with the Permissions API. New headless mode closed most of these gaps. A software graphics renderer and a default 800 by 600 window can still stand out.

web.api: navigator.plugins.length; navigator.languages; window.outerWidth; Notification.permission vs permissions.query({name:'notifications'}); WebGL renderer; window.chrome

steps: Page script reads window, navigator and permission values
Script cross checks them against each other
Mismatches add to a bot score

fields.name: Notification.permission vs permissions.query
fields.range: denied vs prompt mismatch in older headless Chrome

fields.name: WebGL renderer
fields.range: software renderer such as SwiftShader on servers

limits.headline: Can tell when the page has no real desktop behind it
limits.user_action: Nothing. Page script runs when the page loads
can: Compare window size, plugins and languages with what a desktop shows
Compare two permission answers that should match
Notice a software graphics renderer on a server
Raise a bot score from several small mismatches
cannot: Prove automation from any one value
Catch new headless mode on its own
See what the agent is doing
Resist a stealth plugin that patches each value
limits.differs: Newer Chrome builds fixed several of these. A stealth plugin can patch the rest, so sites treat them as weak clues and combine them.

story.what_it_is: A set of tiny oddities that a screenless browser leaves behind when its values do not agree with each other.

marketing.name: Headless Chrome
marketing.pitch: Docs describe Chrome running without a visible UI; no page window exists.

story.for_you: You never see it. A normal browser agrees with itself everywhere, so nothing happens. A headless agent can fail a few small tests.
story.for_makers: Treat each value as a weak hint. Contradictions between values (a permission that says denied in one API and prompt in another) are stronger than any single value. Re check after Chrome releases, because defaults change.

use_cases.example: A bot filter compares two permission answers and flags a mismatch.
A sneaker shop challenges clients with no plugins and no languages.
An ad verifier drops views from clients with a software graphics renderer on a datacenter.
A browser game checks window size to catch bots that run without a screen.
Analytics filters visits with a zero sized window.
A tester runs a detection page to see how their headless setup looks.

risks: False positives for people on unusual setups

technical_bounds: Several values changed in newer headless mode
A real server hosted desktop browser can show some of them

history.change: Headless mode ships with several values that differ from headed Chrome
New headless mode brings it much closer to headed Chrome
